newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 27.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:

* NEW YORK - Key awards at the annual Grammy Awards, held Wednesday at Madison Square Garden, went to mainstream pop. "Change the World," performed by Eric Clapton in the John Travolta film "Phenomenon," was record of the year and song of the year. Producer-songwriter-singer Babyface went into the evening's competition with 12 nominations, more than any other nominee, but took just three awards.

* HOLLYWOOD - General Electric's NBC won its ninth straight sweeps victory, courtesy of "Asteroid" and "Schindler's List," but overall the combined household and demo averages of CBS, NBC, Fox and Disney-owned ABC were off from the 1996 February sweep. While NBC dominated in households and the key 18-49 and 25-54 demos as well as total viewers, News Corp's Fox was also strong, with a record performance and second-place finish in the 18-49 race. Fox was the only network to improve in the key demo groups and households. Westinghouse's CBS nabbed second place in households.

* NEW YORK - Viacom's Paramount and Sydney Pollack's Mirage Enterprises have made a deal for Michael Tolkin to direct the comedy "20 Billion," which Tolkin wrote with Stephen Gaghan and Michael Perry that appears to satirize billionaires Bill Gates and Warren Buffett. Tolkin will be paid in the seven figures for writing and directing once the studio greenlights the film.

* LONDON - At least 17 serious bidders, including most of the biggest names in the U.K. film industry, will apply Friday for the four British film production franchises to be funded by the national lottery. This hugely ambitious initiative is designed to trigger a revolution in the British film industry, by using public money to create a miniature version of the Hollywood studio system.

* HOLLYWOOD - A Sharon Stone remake of "Gloria," the 1980 John Cassavetes picture that won an Oscar nomination for Gena Rowlands, is being unveiled by Sony Corp's Mandalay Pictures to foreign buyers for distribution at the American Film Market, which opens Thursday in Santa Monica.

* NEW YORK - Seven months after joining Disney's Miramax Films in the new post of president of production and television, Allen Sabinson is departing by mutual agreement with company co-chairmen Harvey and Bob Weinstein and reportedly has a deal with another studio for an executive slot. Miramax confirmed Sabinson's exit on Wednesday. However, just where he was exiting to remained unclear. Sabinson would not comment. Friday is his last day.
